claims.text: Reducing or altering surface non-metallic inclusions such as MnS on pre-exposure Q235 steel will suppress localized-corrosion onset and progression in chloride-containing environments.
Surface inclusions on Q235 accelerate pitting by forming micro-galvanic cells.
Pre-exposure Q235 steel has native surface inclusions including MnS.
The native inclusions are uniformly distributed over the Q235 surface.
Electropolishing or local surface treatment can selectively remove or alter non-metallic inclusions on Q235 steel.
A standardized secondary polishing step is intended to make treated and untreated samples similar in surface roughness.
Treated and untreated samples will be compared in stirred 3.5 wt.% NaCl at approximately 25 °C and 80 °C.
The density and distribution of non-metallic inclusions constitute the structural mediator governing corrosion behavior.
Localized electrochemical heterogeneities can concentrate pitting and selective corrosion in particular microstructural regions.
Distinct surface regions can behave as local anodes and cathodes during chloride corrosion.
Non-metallic inclusions specifically serve as pit-initiation sites on bare Q235 steel.
Reducing inclusions minimizes micro-galvanic coupling between inclusions and the steel matrix.
Minimizing inclusion–matrix micro-galvanic coupling will delay pit initiation and reduce overall corrosion rate.
The inclusion-reduced sample will exhibit delayed pitting relative to untreated Q235.
The inclusion-reduced sample will have lower pit density and pit depth than untreated Q235.
The inclusion-reduced sample will have a lower overall corrosion rate than untreated Q235.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to stirred chloride-rich aqueous environments at approximately 25 °C and 80 °C.
No statistically significant corrosion improvement despite verified inclusion reduction would falsify the proposed governing role of surface inclusions.

contradictions.description: The intervention and uncertainty fields require comparable or identical final roughness, but the design applies secondary polishing to the treated set while saying the reference set is left untreated with its native roughness. This does not clearly control roughness and could confound inclusion content with surface finish.
